instruction.name: movfr2gr.d
instruction.description: Move the 64 bits of fj into rd.

latencies.notes: 2 cycles for this direction. The split between the two directions is not observable on this core: every closed chain crosses the boundary both ways, so only the sum shows up (the round trip measures 4.00 cycles and stays additive). The split is fixed by the microarchitecture: an FPR load cannot take the address-bypass path, so `fld.d $f0, $r4, 0; movfr2gr.d $r4, $f0` (6.98 cycles) has to be a 5-cycle load plus a 2-cycle move, and the 4.00-cycle FPR round trip then puts the other direction at 2. The stored experiment is the round trip itself, with the opposite direction subtracted as chain_latency.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.asm: movfr2gr.d $r12, $f0; movfr2gr.d $r13, $f1; movfr2gr.d $r14, $f2; movfr2gr.d $r15, $f3; movfr2gr.d $r16, $f4; movfr2gr.d $r17, $f5; movfr2gr.d $r18, $f6; movfr2gr.d $r19, $f7

notes: Individual FPR->GPR latency is 3 cycles. Round trip with movgr2fr.d is 4 cycles; high-half round trip movgr2frh.w + movfrh2gr.s is 5 cycles. 3+2 cycles for movgr2fr/movfr2gr is incompatible with the 4-cycle full round trip. Throughput is 1 CPI for 1-20 independent lanes.
